fields.topology_type: Source-synchronous low-power mobile memory bus. The controller (master) drives the quarter-speed CK, the 7-bit DDR CA bus, CS, and on-demand full-speed WCK to one or more LPDDR5 SDRAM devices (slaves) per channel; the DRAM drives RDQS during reads. Mobile LPDDR5 is soldered directly to the SoC board (or PoP-stacked), typically as a two-channel (x16 per channel) package with an internal two-deck organization. There is no removable DIMM and no CKE pin.

supported_topologies.name: Single controller + single LPDDR5 die
supported_topologies.description: Point-to-point on the SoC board / PoP; one x16 channel directly attached.

supported_topologies.name: Single controller + multi-die LPDDR5 package
supported_topologies.description: Multiple dies in one package; per-channel CS and clocks select dies.

supported_topologies.name: Two-channel x16 package
supported_topologies.description: Two independent x16 channels per package, each with its own CK/WCK/RDQS/CA/CS/DQ/DMI.

supported_topologies.name: Package-on-Package (PoP) over the AP
supported_topologies.description: LPDDR5 stacked on top of the mobile application processor.

master_slave_role_summary.description: Generates quarter-speed CK and on-demand full-speed WCK; issues all commands on the CA bus; performs WCK2CK synchronization; tracks per-bank state; manages refresh (ab/pb), ZQ calibration, read/write training, link ECC, DBI, DVFS; sources DQ on writes and sinks DQ on reads.

Decodes commands from the 7-bit DDR CA bus; opens/closes rows (two-ACT); locks internal WCK to CK during WCK2CK sync; drives DQ + RDQS on reads and sinks DQ + DMI on writes; generates internal refresh; supports deep sleep and CA-bus-bounded power-down.

fields.interconnect_role: There is no LPDDR5-protocol-layer interconnect (no router / bridge). The bus is a flat 1-controller : N-device per-channel bus. Device selection is via CS; within a device, bank/bank-group selection is via BG/BA fields; within a bank, row/column is via the CA address fields. Channels are independent.

ordering_guarantees.within_a_burst: 16 (BL16) or 32 (BL32) beats in the order set by the LPDDR5 column addressing (B0-B3 / C0-C5); RD32 may start at a position within the 32-word-aligned burst via C0 / B3.
ordering_guarantees.across_commands: Commands are committed in the order issued; tCCD_L/tRRD_L (same bank group) and tCCD_S/tRRD_S (different bank group), tFAW, and refresh timing serialize commands on the wire; every high-speed transfer requires a prior WCK2CK sync.

fields.memory_vs_peripheral_regions: The LPDDR5 SDRAM exposes a linear DRAM array as a bank-group × bank × row × column address space plus a mode-register space accessed via MRW/MRR. Mode-register and ZQ/training commands use the same CA bus but do not access the DRAM array.

device_classification.soldered_LPDDR5_die: Standalone LPDDR5 x16 die soldered / PoP-stacked on the mobile SoC board.
device_classification.multi_die_package: Multiple LPDDR5 dies in one package (per-channel CS / clocks).
device_classification.LPDDR5_controller: Controller + PHY IP integrated into the mobile SoC / application processor.
device_classification.two_deck_device: LPDDR5 device implementing the two-deck internal organization for finer power/access granularity.

default_signal_values_evidence_tables: Bank-group / bank organization (16 banks, 4 bank groups)
